title: Broken Retaining Wall
description: A thick limestone retaining wall with a central collapse, fractured ashlar, exposed rubble core and a debris fan.

review.notes: Rebuild round 1 of 2. Fixed: real ashlar coursing with dark mortar joints, two broken remnants with stepped, collapsed tops, a breach with fallen blocks and a turf strip at the foot (hero, t9). Still failing: (1) material 7: every block is the same clean, even pale grey with crisp chamfers; no weathering gradient (rain streaks, darker damp lower courses, lichen on top surfaces, mortar loss) as on the approved bridge and stair. (2) form_detail/defects 7: the exposed rubble core is a pile of small, pale, sharp faceted shards that read as crushed ice or crystals (closeup, t8), not lime-bound rubble; and all blocks are flat-faced boxes with the same chamfer, no spalled corners or rounded wear. Fix: reuse the approved weathering stack from the bridge/stair on the wall (streaks under the broken tops, damp band and moss on the lowest two courses, lichen on upper faces); make the core darker grey-brown mortar with embedded rounded and broken stones of mixed size; chip and round a third of the block corners and vary block tone slightly.
